description: Rapid linear peeled transfers along a single chain: funds hop through a short chain of fresh intermediate wallets before reaching the final target.
Swap volatile assets into a stablecoin on the origin chain, then bridge the proceeds to a target chain before final transfer to the destination wallet.
One-to-N splitting: the source fans funds out into multiple parallel intermediate nodes on the same chain, which later converge into an aggregator before the final target.
Layered chain hopping across three distinct chains: funds bridge from chain A to chain B, then immediately bridge again to chain C, where they are finally transferred to the target.
N-to-1 integration: several source streams merge into a single aggregator node, which then transfers the consolidated funds to the final target.
Asset conversion through a decentralized exchange liquidity pool: funds are transferred into a swap node and converted into a different asset before reaching the target.
Deep layered peeling chain: a long sequence of linear hops through intermediate wallets on one chain, maximising the number of hops before reaching the target.
Round-trip bridging: funds leave the origin chain through a bridge, pass through an intermediate chain, and are bridged back to the origin chain before final settlement.
Mixer-style anonymisation: funds are swapped through an asset-conversion node, split into parallel streams, and merged back into an aggregator before the final target.
Repeated same-chain asset conversions: funds are swapped through multiple conversion nodes in sequence to obfuscate the asset trail before the final transfer.
Cross-chain layered integration: two source streams merge on the origin chain and are bridged to the target chain, where they merge again with a local stream before settlement.
Split-then-bridge fan-out: funds are split into parallel streams on the origin chain and each stream is bridged to a different destination chain before re-converging on the final target chain.

Iterative peeling chain: a source or continuation node splits value asymmetrically into a dominant continuation edge and a minor peel edge; the continuation repeats the split and minor peel edges terminate at targets.

Source distributes incoming funds via multiple split edges to a first layer of intermediate nodes, each of which further splits funds to additional intermediate nodes, forming a layered fan-out distribution structure.
Funds from multiple sources merge into a mixer aggregator, then are split into fragmented withdrawals to targets, breaking the link between deposit and withdrawal.
Cross-chain bridge hop to a less-monitored chain, optionally preceded by asset conversion, followed by transfer through a reconstructed destination address.
Multiple victim source accounts merge chaotic irregular inflows into one or few attacker core aggregation wallets, forming consolidation peaks; source accounts are victims and not part of the gang.
Illicit crypto flows fragmented across source branches converge into an OTC/P2P intermediary aggregator, then convert to fiat or privacy assets and exit to an off-chain target.
Cross-chain asset conversions and bridges from multiple source chains merge into a consolidation-chain aggregator.
Multi-chain stolen funds are swapped into a common asset on their source chains and bridged into an Ethereum aggregator for consolidation.
Synthetic asset is created without backing, consolidated from multiple source outputs, then moved across a federated bridge to a destination chain where it becomes a native asset.
Abstract cross-chain escape: multiple illicit asset origins on the source chain are merged into an aggregator, bridged to a target chain, and then transferred to an attacker-controlled target.
Consolidation of source-chain proceeds via merge, followed by cross-chain bridge to a destination-chain aggregator.
Unauthorized asset created on sidechain is transferred then bridged out via peg-out to native chain and transferred to target.

Attacker-controlled source on Chain_A initiates a cross-chain bridge request and exploits bridge notarization to inject a false state root, causing the bridge on Chain_B to release drained assets to the attacker's target address.
Source funds are swapped through a thin liquidity pool into a low-value asset, then split to multiple attacker-controlled withdrawal positions.
Proceeds from multiple asset types are swapped into a common intermediate asset and then swapped again into a final holding asset, obscuring the original asset trail.
Cross-chain bridge from source chain to destination chain followed by internal transfer to an intermediate wallet.
Multiple asset conversions through liquidity pools obscure the origin of drained value before profit extraction.
Flash-loan-funded acquisition of a token, swap into the token, exploitation of a burn-before-sync pool mechanism to inflate price, swap back to the base asset, and transfer to a cash-out service.

Repeated batched asset swaps within a pool vault are used to create rounding-induced pricing deviations; the attacker cycles and converts pooled assets to inflate an internal balance before withdrawal.
Attacker repeatedly swaps among pool assets to obfuscate value and inflate internal balances before withdrawing funds.
Source provides assets to an intermediate actor; the intermediate actor performs a swap at an asset conversion venue; the conversion venue forwards proceeds to a target aggregator.
Attacker uses multiple funded addresses to purchase tokens from a liquidity pool, fanning out fund flow to fabricate volume and obscure origin.
Rug pull proceeds from multiple victim and attacker addresses flow through a liquidity pool and are consolidated into a central fund-holding address via a chain of intermediate transfers.

Fund-holding source routes funds through a shared infrastructure contract, which splits them across many intermediate recipient addresses; these recipients then swap into tokens via a DEX/router to simulate trading volume.
Multiple source wallets consolidate operational funds into an intermediate fund-holding address, which then transfers to a deployer account for rug-pull token deployment.

Rug pull cash-out: external funding supports token deployment and liquidity provision; pooled victim funds are then converted through a DEX router by removing liquidity or dumping tokens, and the resulting base asset is transferred to the attacker target.
Unbacked sidechain asset is minted, bridged to a second chain via peg-out, then split between a federation aggregator and an attacker-controlled target.
Unbacked asset created on a sidechain is moved via a peg-out bridge to a main chain, then split between a returned portion and a retained portion.
